author: Russell Brand
description: Russell's guest broke down how the Wellcome Trust, led at the time by Sir Jeremy Farrar, made around ten billion dollars during the pandemic thanks to its heavy investment portfolio, including stakes in pharmaceutical companies and even the food delivery app DoorDash, while Farrar himself was instrumental in pushing for lockdowns. He connected this directly to Professor Neil Ferguson's now infamous Report 9 out of Imperial College London, itself heavily funded by the Gates Foundation, the paper used to justify locking down much of the world, predicting millions of deaths in the US and half a million in the UK without lockdowns. He pointed out that a US Vaccine Task Force official cited that exact paper when questioned by reporters about the sudden need for lockdowns, despite the underlying computer model never being peer reviewed, never publicly disclosed, and based on flawed exponential growth assumptions. author: Russell Brand
description:
Russell reacts to Robert F. Kennedy Jr. laying out the disturbing claims from his book about Anthony Fauci, admitting that even he found some of it hard to believe until RFK broke down exactly why the truth gets buried. RFK draws a chilling parallel to Ignaz Semmelweis, the 1855 doctor who proved handwashing saved lives and was rewarded with ridicule, an asylum, and an early death instead of praise. The pattern repeats itself throughout history, RFK argues, and this clip makes it painfully clear why the people who tell the truth are always the ones who get destroyed for it. A must watch for anyone who has ever wondered why the loudest whistleblowers so rarely get their flowers.

author: Russell Brand
description: Russell reacted to reports of microneedle patch implants funded by the Gates Foundation, essentially a small comb-like device pressed into the skin that installs quantum dots detectable by smartphones, floated as a possible future vaccine passport system that wouldn't even require a phone, just a scan of your skin. Russell leaned fully into the satire, joking that Bill Gates finally gets his moment of revenge after a nerdish school reputation, now armed with lipid nanoparticles instead of a dodgeball target on his back. He pivoted into a more serious point though, admitting that even claims from Robert F. Kennedy Jr.'s book that once sounded too extreme to believe kept turning out to have some grounding. His guest connected it to a much older pattern in public health, using the story of Ignaz Semmelweis, a doctor in 1850s Vienna who discovered handwashing dramatically reduced infection deaths, only to be mocked, discredited, and eventually institutionalized for it. author: Russell Brand
description:
Russell's guest broke down the Kissinger Report, in which Henry Kissinger reportedly identified countries like Puerto Rico and the Philippines as needing reduced population growth so their resources could remain available to America down the line. He argued this kind of long-term planning, stretching well beyond any single four or eight year presidential term, proves that real power doesn't actually sit with elected leadership, it sits within the systems themselves. He posed a direct question, whether the pandemic may have always been connected to the same kind of population thinking revealed decades earlier. His conclusion was blunt, if governments are really just administrators managing populations on behalf of something bigger, then people need to unite and propose entirely new systems of their own, starting with direct democracy. Sometimes the most unsettling documents are the ones written in plain language decades before anyone was paying attention.
